inputBoundaryInventory.summary: The audit target is a web service, so the untrusted-input boundary is HTTP: (1) THE dominant source is the Flask route path-converter variable: @app.route("/<path:path>", methods=[...]) at xhu.py:104/:189/:214 binds the Werkzeug `path` converter result to the put_file/head_file/get_file parameter `path` - the converter captures the ENTIRE remainder of the request URL (slashes included) AFTER Werkzeug percent-decoding, so the handler receives a fully attacker-controlled, URL-decoded multi-segment path string; it flows into sanitized_join(path, pathlib.Path(app.config["DATA_ROOT"])) (:64-67 via get_info, :107-110 directly) -> result = (root / path).absolute() (:43) -> the startswith prefix guard (:44) -> get_paths '<base>.data'/'<base>.meta' companions (:50-51) -> dest_path.parent.mkdir (:137), write_file at.open('xb') (:76), at.unlink() rollback (:80), metadata_file.open('x') (:144), data_file.stat() (:197), and flask.send_file(str(data_file)) (:228). For PUT the path is additionally gated by an HMAC: hmac_input = '{} {}'.format(path, length) signed with the operator SECRET_KEY and compared to the request's 'v' query parameter (xhu.py:118-130) - i.e. an uploader must present a server-authorized HMAC over the exact path+length; GET/HEAD have NO such gate, so the read-side path is fully unauthenticated (this trust asymmetry is recorded as boundary evidence, not a verdict). (2) flask.request.args.get("v", "") at :118 - query-string verification key, consumed only by hmac.compare_digest, never used as a path. (3) flask.request.headers.get("Content-Length", 0) at :119 (int-coerced, feeds the HMAC input and the stream copy length) and flask.request.headers.get("Content-Type", ...) at :132-135 (stored into the metadata JSON, later replayed as response headers). (4) the flask.request.stream body object at :142 - the raw PUT payload read by stream_file (:92-101) and written into the data file. (5) Operator-configured values that are NOT attacker-controlled and are NOT emitted as source rows: app.config.from_envvar("XMPP_HTTP_UPLOAD_CONFIG") (:34 - deployment config file location from the environment), app.config["DATA_ROOT"] reads (:66/:109/:194/:219 - the containment base directory), app.config["SECRET_KEY"] (:121), app.config['ENABLE_CORS'] (:37), app.config.get("NON_ATTACHMENT_MIME_TYPES", []) (:178 - the operator's mimetype glob allowlist). DATA_ROOT appears only as the base operand of path construction (emitted as path_ctor sink rows, not as a source). No CLI arguments, no message-queue consumers, no database reads, no other environment-variable reads exist in the audited code.

guardAndTraversalEvidence: Base-directory containment guard: sanitized_join (xhu.py:42-46) computes result = (root / path).absolute() and accepts only if str(result).startswith(str(root) + "/"), else ValueError (caught as 404 at :111-116/:198-203/:221-226) - a STRING-PREFIX check, applied to the joined path object

Canonicalization gap evidence: the guard path uses .absolute() only - there is NO pathlib .resolve()/.is_symlink(), NO os.path.realpath/normpath, NO explicit '..' segment rejection, and NO basename-only extraction anywhere in xhu.py; Path.absolute() makes the path absolute without resolving symlinks (and performs no textual normalization of '..' segments in the CPython implementations targeted by this project's python3 classifiers), so the prefix comparison runs on the un-normalized joined string - recorded as CWE-22/23/36-relevant guard evidence for the labeling and analysis steps, no vulnerability verdict assumed

Symlink/TOCTOU evidence (CWE-36/59-adjacent): the sanitized_join check and the later filesystem use are separate operations - put_file checks, then mkdir(parents=True) at :137 then at.open('xb') at :76; head/get check, then data_file.stat() at :197 / flask.send_file at :228; a symlink planted inside DATA_ROOT after the check would redirect the open (the check-then-use window is recorded; put_file's exclusive-create modes 'xb'/'x' with EEXIST->409 (:157-163) and the at.unlink() rollback (:79-81) limit overwrite semantics but not redirection)

Mixed-separator evidence: no backslash normalization or separator handling exists anywhere in xhu.py; on POSIX a backslash is an ordinary filename character, and Werkzeug's routing percent-decodes %5C and %2E before the handler sees the path (framework-provided decoding - no explicit decode/encode calls exist in the app code)

Directory creation from URL components: dest_path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True, mode=0o770) at :137 creates every intermediate directory of the uploaded path under DATA_ROOT (arbitrary subdirectory creation, exists_ok tolerated)

HMAC authorization asymmetry: only put_file authenticates its input (verification key 'v' = HMAC-SHA256 over '{} {}'.format(path, length) with the operator SECRET_KEY, xhu.py:118-130); head_file and get_file apply the sanitized_join guard but no authentication - the read-side path is unauthenticated

Filename derivation: the stored file name and its .data/.meta companions derive entirely from the URL path (get_paths at :49-53 appends the '.data'/'.meta' suffixes); there is no multipart filename, no Content-Disposition filename parsing, no archive entry handling

Post-storage metadata replay: the Content-Type supplied by the uploader (:132-135) is persisted in the .meta JSON and replayed into responses by generate_headers (:173-186) with Content-Disposition: attachment unless the operator's NON_ATTACHMENT_MIME_TYPES globs match (fnmatch at :179) - header-injection-adjacent, out of Pass 1 path scope, recorded for completeness
